title: Structured JSON output is sometimes truncated at the tail
description: Some structured generations end with a dangling comma or half-written field, and downstream parsing fails instead of recovering conservatively. The failures are intermittent and usually show up after longer generations where the raw text looks almost valid except for the final few characters.
expected_behavior: The workflow should either recover a valid JSON prefix or retry cleanly with a larger token budget.

  parsed = safe_json_loads(raw_text)

  raise JSONDecodeError(...)

title: Need to verify whether stale artifact cleanup can hide previous debugging evidence
description: We remove previous artifacts before each run. On successful runs that is fine, but on failed reruns it becomes hard to compare the previous output directory with the current one because cleanup already deleted it. We should triage whether this behavior is localized and explicit enough.
expected_behavior: Cleanup should be explicit and localized so it is easy to reason about when previous artifacts are deleted.
log_excerpt: reset_run_outputs removed /tmp/runs/issue_a before rerun; previous diff artifacts no longer available after failure
stacktrace_excerpt:
File "run_bug_triage_workflow.py", line 63, in main
  reset_run_outputs(args.output, artifact_dir)
File "structured_agent/script_utils.py", line 118, in reset_run_outputs
  shutil.rmtree(artifact_dir)

title: Very long cases fail inside vLLM with a decoder prompt length error instead of a preflight budget check
description: When long mixed-corpus cases run, the process can spend a few minutes preparing stage prompts and then die with a ValueError similar to 'decoder prompt length 11404 is longer than maximum model length 8192'. The failure currently arrives from the model backend instead of being caught earlier with a clearer message.
expected_behavior: The runtime should detect prompt length pressure with the tokenizer before handing an impossible request to vLLM.
log_excerpt: ValueError: The decoder prompt (length 11404) is longer than the maximum model length of 8192
stacktrace_excerpt:
File "structured_agent/engine.py", line 83, in _generate_once
  outputs = self.llm.generate(...)
File "vllm/entrypoints/llm.py", line 1700, in _add_request
  raise ValueError(...)

title: Compression sometimes does not trigger for CJK-heavy history because the fallback token estimate is too optimistic
description: Several long Chinese or mixed-language cases look comfortably below the 4k trigger when we use the rough estimate, but the real tokenizer count is much higher. That means compressed-history skips compression until it is already too late or never activates on the intended stage boundary.
expected_behavior: Fallback token estimation should be conservative enough that multilingual text does not badly undershoot the real tokenizer length.
log_excerpt: history estimate=3960, real tokenizer count≈8100, compression skipped before decision stage
stacktrace_excerpt:
File "structured_agent/utils.py", line 142, in count_tokens_simple
  return len(text) // 4
File "structured_agent/transfer_methods/common.py", line 521, in compress_history
  if history_tokens < min_history_tokens: skip

title: Shared completion proxy still assumes the old four-stage skeleton
description: We now have workflows with five or more stages, but if a new workflow forgets to override the completion proxy locally, the shared helper still scores only the historical constraints/candidate/decision/review slots. That makes utility-at-SLO and progress-style metrics look misleadingly low or oddly shaped.
expected_behavior: The baseline completion helper should be safer for non-four-stage workflows or make the override requirement impossible to miss.
log_excerpt: completion_proxy stayed at 0.50 after signal/query/evidence stages completed in a six-stage workflow
stacktrace_excerpt: File "structured_agent/state_transfer.py", line 221, in completion_proxy\n  if artifacts.constraints_state: score += 0.20\n  if artifacts.candidate_state: score += 0.30

title: Support runs can print the wrong summary block when the printer only distinguishes cases from issues
description: After adding support tickets, one of the summary printers still decided between a legacy case-style output path and the bug-style output path using only the presence of 'cases'. Ticket runs then fell through to the issue branch, which made the console summary omit the support-specific metrics we actually care about.
expected_behavior: Summary printing should recognize support-ticket runs explicitly and show ticket-specific quality metrics.
log_excerpt: Generated summary omitted ticket metrics and printed issue-oriented counts for a support run
stacktrace_excerpt: File "structured_agent/eval.py", line 612, in print_summary\n  if 'cases' in summary: ... else: print_bug_triage_summary(summary)

title: Support ticket reports need a dedicated quality block instead of reusing legacy case assumptions
description: The generic report writer worked fine for an earlier case-oriented workflow, but once support metrics were added we still needed to expose issue type, eligibility, resolution, and escalation matches. Using only that legacy branch made the report much harder to inspect during experiments.
expected_behavior: Report generation should render support-ticket quality fields with a dedicated support-aware block.
log_excerpt: support report lacked issue type / eligibility / resolution lines even though quality metrics were present in result json

title: Compressed-history bug triage still pays the full repo-evidence cost before any compression can happen
description: On larger triage issues with many retrieved snippets, the expensive part is often the first evidence-heavy stage. Right now compressed-history starts helping only after that point, so long triage cases can look surprisingly similar to full-history exactly where the biggest read cost happens.
expected_behavior: The workflow should make that policy tradeoff explicit and easy to tune when the first heavy stage becomes the main bottleneck.
log_excerpt: compress_before_hypothesis_shortlist fired, but evidence_screen had already consumed ~5k context tokens from repo snippets
